General
As a leading strategic partner to government, Maximus helps improve the delivery of public services amid complex technology, health, economic, and social challenges. Maximus provides tech-enabled services to government agencies, including innovative business process management and technology solutions that are designed to improve outcomes for the public and create higher levels of productivity and efficiency of government-sponsored programs. With a deep understanding of program service delivery, acute insights that achieve operational excellence, and an extensive awareness of the needs of the people being served, our employees advance the critical missions of our partners.
Through our mission of Moving Technology, People and Government Forward , we have a record of creating value for our customers by equipping our leaders with best-in-class technology to implement government policies. We efficiently operate programs using a combination of this technology and a robust and reliable labor sourcing capability and network, provided predominantly to our customers through performance-based cost models.
Our past and future success is based upon our strategic priorities that we believe are aligned with long-term demand characteristics and bipartisan programs that shape the role of government in serving its citizens. Our strategic priorities include:
• Tech-Enabled Government Service Delivery. Delivering citizen services in an innovation ecosystem that drives measurable outcomes and unlocks the full potential of an agency's mission through data-driven insights.
• Future of Health. Automating complex processes and empowering health professionals with timely, actionable data - enabling them to focus on individuals while responding to community needs at scale.
• Technological Modernization. Modernizing programs and legacy technology systems to be agile enough to meet the needs of a rapidly changing landscape and aligning solutions around the unique circumstances of each program.
This strategy aligns with our near-term priorities, including expanding within U.S. federal markets, such as defense and national security; advanced and scaled deployment of AI into our operations; and capturing opportunities to support states as they address the implementation of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in the United States.
Our Business Segments
We operate our business through three segments: U.S. Federal Services, U.S. Services, and Outside the U.S.
U.S. Federal Services Segment
Our U.S. Federal Services Segment delivers solutions that help various U.S. federal government agencies better execute their mission, including program operations and management, contact centers, clinical services, and advanced technology solutions.
This segment serves a broad range of federal government agencies, many of whom we have long-term relationships with, such as the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS), the U.S. Department of Education, and the Internal Revenue Service.
We deliver clinical services, including independent assessments of benefit eligibility. Most notably, we provide medical disability examinations on behalf of the VA, administering evaluations through a large network of experienced clinicians focused on serving veterans. Other health eligibility and enrollment services include arbitration, appeals support and payment resolution.
We deliver Business Process Services (BPS), including eligibility and enrollment, outreach and other services for federal health and human services programs. This work includes our contract with CMS to manage contact centers, supporting the federal marketplace for the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and providing the primary engagement center for Medicare through 1-800-MEDICARE.
We provide an independent and conflict-free service assisting borrowers with Department of Education-originated loans.

We provide technology solutions across a range of federal agencies that are designed to advance agency missions through operating, modernizing, and improving existing platforms. These services include delivering automated systems and upgrades, and the integration and management of disparate systems and processes. We supplement these services with additional expertise in AI and advanced analytics, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure and data management to fulfill client needs while ensuring compliance with security regulations and best practices.
A small number of U.S. federal agencies provide the majority of this segment’s revenue. There is no significant seasonality in this segment’s revenue, although certain contracts may experience an increase in volume tied to benefit open enrollment periods, typically towards the end of the calendar year. Other fluctuations may arise from volume variations or program maturity, with contracts typically recording lower revenue and profitability in the early phases of the arrangement.
Our primary competitors in this segment are typically other large, U.S. based federal government contractors, information technology (IT) firms and consultants.
U.S. Services Segment
Our U.S. Services Segment provides program operations, contact centers, clinical services, employment services, advanced technology solutions, and related professional services for U.S. state and local government programs. These services support a variety of programs, including those under Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, state-based marketplaces established under the ACA, Temporary Assistance to Needy Families, and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). During fiscal year 2026, we divested our child support management services business.
The core of our work is providing comprehensive program administration services for government health benefit programs. We are the largest provider of Medicaid eligibility support and enrollment services, and one of the largest providers of application and enrollment support for state-based health insurance marketplaces. In administering health benefit programs such as Medicaid, Maximus does not make the final determination of eligibility.
The services we provide to each state or locality vary from contract to contract but typically include:
• Centralized, AI-enabled multilingual customer contact centers serving telephone, mail or digital customers across a range of state programs;
• Application assistance and independent health plan choice counselling to beneficiaries to help them access benefits and make informed choices;
• Beneficiary outreach, education, eligibility assistance, enrollment, credentialling and redetermination services; and
• The administration of programs that provide subsidized telephone and internet services for eligible customers.
We provide clinical services to some of the largest state administered programs in the United States, primarily in the form of person-centered assessments for long-term care services. These services include level-of-care assessments, plan-of-care assessments, pre-admission screening and resident reviews.
We provide employment services in a number of states. These services vary between locations but may include eligibility support, case management, job-readiness preparation, job search and employer outreach, job retention and career advancement, and selected educational and training services, including vocational training.
We offer technology solutions that help government agencies improve program accuracy, modernize operations, and manage technology risk. These solutions include Accuracy Assistant SM , our AI-enabled accuracy platform, and independent verification and validation services that provide independent technology oversight and quality assurance to help ensure systems meet requirements.
The balance of this segment’s work includes various specialized services, such as services to assist clients in their procurement, business process assessment and design, implementation, quality assurance, policy and procedure reviews and management of systems and projects through independent project management. We provide cost allocation services for local jurisdictions seeking state and federal funding, as well as audit assistance and grant and proposal reviews. In some states, we provide services allowing the public to review the profiles of licensed health care providers in that state. We assist commercial customers in claiming workforce and location-based tax benefits. Finally, we support website design and development services.

risks:
Our operations are subject to many risks that could adversely affect our future financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows, and, therefore, the market value of our securities. The risks described below highlight some of the factors that have affected and, in the future, could affect our operations. Additional risks we do not yet know of or that we currently think are immaterial may also affect our business operations. If any of the events or circumstances described in the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, or results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
Risks Pertaining to Our Client Relationships
We rely on key contracts with federal, state, and local governments for a significant portion of our revenue. A substantial reduction in those contracts would materially adversely affect our operating results.
In fiscal year 2026, approximately 56% of our total revenue was derived from the U.S. federal government, and approximately 34% of our total revenue was derived from contracts with state and local government agencies. Any significant disruption or deterioration in our relationship with federal, state, and local governments and a corresponding reduction in these contracts would significantly reduce our revenue and could substantially harm our business.
In fiscal year 2026, approximately 60% of our revenue came from our ten largest contracts. Furthermore, approximately one-fifth of our revenue came from contracts with a single federal agency. If any of our current significant contracts or significant contracts we enter into in the future were terminated or modified, such that the modified contract resulted in an unfavorable financial impact or our scope or volume of work under those contracts was decreased, our revenue and net income could significantly decline. Additional potential impacts of the loss of a significant contract or contracts, such as our rebid with the VA, might include impairment charges related to tangible and intangible assets, including goodwill. Our success will depend on our continued ability to develop and manage relationships with significant customers and there is no assurance that we will be able to diversify our customer base in the near future, or at all.
The markets in which we sell our services are served by a relatively small number of governmental agencies, which limits the number of potential customers. We cannot provide assurance that we will be able to retain our largest customers, that we will be able to attract additional customers, or that our customers will continue to buy our services in the same volume as in prior years. The loss of one or more of our largest customers, any reduction or delay in sales to these customers, our inability to successfully develop relationships with additional customers, or future price concessions could impact our business.
Our contracts typically run for a fixed number of years and may be extended for an additional specified number of years if the contracting entity or its agent elects to do so. When these contracts expire, they may be opened for bidding to competing bidders, and there is no guarantee that the contracts will be renewed or extended. Our clients may elect to open bidding processes earlier than anticipated, resulting in increased competition prior to the anticipated end of contracts.
Our reputation and relationships with our clients are key factors in maintaining our business. Negative press reports or publicity, regardless of accuracy, could harm our reputation. If our reputation is negatively affected, our clients may decrease or cease business with us. In addition, we are subject to various reviews, audits, and investigations to verify our compliance with the terms of our contracts, as well as compliance with applicable laws and regulations. Any adverse review, audit, or investigation could result in, among other things, cancellation of contracts; refunding of amounts that have been paid pursuant to contracts; imposition of fines, penalties, and other sanctions; loss of rights to participate on various programs; loss of licenses; lowered quality ratings; or changes to the way we do business. In addition, under government procurement regulations and practices, a negative determination from a government audit could result in a contractor being fined, debarred, and/or suspended from being able to bid on, or be awarded new government contracts for a period of time.

We obtain most of our business through competitive bidding in response to government Requests For Proposals (RFP). We may not be awarded contracts through this process at the same level in the future as in the past, and contracts we are awarded may not be profitable.
Substantially all of our customers are government agencies. To secure work with government customers, we are often required to respond to competitive government RFPs, and we will only be issued a contract award when we win such a competition. To do so effectively, we must accurately estimate our cost structure for providing the required services, the time required to establish operations, and attempt to submit a proposal that is more advantageous for the client than our competitors' proposals. We must also assemble and submit a large volume of information that must comply with the RFP's rigid requirements and relatively short timetable. Our ability to successfully respond to RFPs could greatly impact our business. There is no assurance that we will continue to be awarded contracts in response to government RFPs, and when we are awarded such contracts, they may not be profitable. The competitive bidding process has substantial costs, including labor costs and management's time to prepare bids and proposals for contracts that may not be awarded to us, may be split among competitors, or that may be awarded but for which we do not receive a meaningful volume of task orders.
In addition, competitors may protest contracts awarded to us through the RFP process that may cause the award to be delayed, cancelled, or require the customer to reinitiate the RFP process. Any loss or delay of start-up and funding of work under protested contract awards may adversely affect our revenues and profitability. In addition, certain of our multiple-award contracts require that we make post-award efforts to obtain task orders under the contract. Because of these factors, we may not be able to obtain task orders or recognize revenue under these multiple-award contracts.
Even where we are an incumbent, our ability to secure continued work or work at similar margins may be affected by competitive rebids or contract changes and cancellations. If we do not win certain recompetes, this may adversely affect our revenue and profitability, potentially resulting in impairment of goodwill and other intangible assets.
